editorialTake:
AI infrastructure is about to become a traded commodity, and that will reshape who holds power in luxury and jewellery. Meta’s $10 billion compute lease talks with Anthropic signal that foundational AI is moving from proprietary advantage to something you can rent, like electricity. At the same time, Very Group is using agentic AI to automate pricing decisions, and Vertu is betting executives will pay $6,880 for a phone with a built-in AI agent. The objection is that luxury and jewellery need human touch and taste, but the evidence shows AI is now a tool for operational leverage, not just creative automation.

The real risk is falling behind as others use AI to optimize margins, speed up launches, or personalize at scale. Research already shows AI’s consumer recommendations for jewellery are flawed, but that gap will close as compute and agentic tools become accessible to anyone with budget. The winners will be those who treat AI capacity as a procurement decision, not a moonshot, and start experimenting now with agentic platforms for pricing, assortment, and clienteling.

For the next quarter, I would assign a team to audit where AI can drive margin or speed, and budget for compute as a line item, before your competitors do. The era of waiting for perfect luxury AI is over. The era of buying and deploying it, piece by piece, has started.
oneSentenceSummary: Meta’s compute leasing overture hints at the imminent emergence of hyperscale AI infrastructure as a traded commodity, upending current power dynamics in foundational models.
